maml:description.maml:para: Creates a read-only exact-version update plan for an installed PowerShell module.

Inspects a compatible installed module in CurrentUser or AllUsers and one registered repository. The target need not be loaded, be the caller, or depend on PSModuleUpdate. PMU is a standalone shared module; consumers own repository configuration and the decision about when to check for updates. Policy defaults to Stable and CurrentUser. Credentials are used only in memory.
`Policy` accepts only `Channel` (`Stable` or `IncludePrerelease`), `Scope` (`CurrentUser` or `AllUsers`), `ExpectedRepositoryUri` (`System.Uri` or null), and `VersionRange` (provider-supported NuGet range string or null). The latter two default to null. IncludePrerelease includes stable releases as well. The explicitly selected scope must already contain the matching name and GUID; PMU never creates a shadow installation or changes scope.
The manifest supplies installed prerelease identity. The legacy `Active*` fields snapshot the supplied module reference and do not imply it is loaded. `RestartRequired` inspects actual loaded copies; PMU never imports the target to plan or apply an update. A plan binds one exact target from one repository and never authorizes a downgrade. Planning does not write locks, staging files, journals, or repository settings.
Choose either `Repository` or `RepositoryUri`, never both. A URI must match exactly one existing registration. The resolved name, endpoint, API version, and trust state are bound into the plan and revalidated before exact discovery, staging, and installation. Removing or repointing that name never causes URI alias selection or fallback to another source.
If the provider does not disclose a package's license-acceptance requirement, the plan conservatively sets `RequiresLicenseAcceptance` to true. Installation then requires explicit `-AcceptLicense`; PMU never interprets absent metadata as permission to accept a license or allow a provider prompt.
Optional per-call provider credential. Supply it again when installing.
One compatible installed module reference; no import or PMU dependency is required. Name and GUID must match its on-disk manifest.
Channel, Scope, ExpectedRepositoryUri (Uri), and VersionRange. Unknown keys are rejected.
One literal registered PSResourceGet repository name.

The absolute endpoint of exactly one existing PSResourceGet registration. Cannot be combined with `Repository`. Unregistered or ambiguous endpoints produce `PMU.RepositoryUnavailable`; PMU never registers a fallback source. Credentials, query strings, and fragments must not be embedded in the URI.

A live schema-1, data-only plan with active and selected-scope installation identity, repository snapshot, exact target, policy, disposition, and prerequisites. It contains no credential and is not a durable authorization token.

maml:alert.maml:para:
Requires PowerShell 7.4 or later and the qualified PSResourceGet 1.2.0 baseline. Missing provider setup, unavailable packages, authentication failures, unsafe paths, and identity mismatches are terminating structured PMU errors, not UpToDate results. Credentials must be supplied independently to installation.
PSResourceGet 1.2.0 Find/Save/Install expose repository names, not a direct URI parameter. This release therefore supports URI selection only through an existing unique registration. Temporary registration is not implemented: the supported APIs persist in a shared user store, provide no operation-local registry or ownership-conditional removal, and cannot guarantee cleanup after process termination. Random names or a PMU-only cooperative lock do not turn those operations into a transaction with other registry writers. PMU performs no production registry writes and creates no stale temporary registrations. On macOS the provider store is under the actual LocalApplicationData `PSResourceGet/PSResourceRepository.xml`; changing HOME alone does not isolate it.
One generic PSResourceGet adapter is used for compatible registered feeds. PSGallery, NuGet.org, Azure Artifacts, and Nexus do not have vendor-specific branches. External-feed behavior requires separate qualification; protocol compatibility is not a live-validation claim.
An unfinished replacement can be planned read-only from a verified recovery backup when a matching active module survives in another version or scope. If no usable module identity survives at all, the mandatory Module parameter cannot be supplied; manual recovery is required.

maml:introduction.maml:para: Creates a stable CurrentUser update plan without changing installed files.

`$installed` is a compatible installed `PSModuleInfo`, not necessarily loaded. The endpoint must already have exactly one registration. General NuGet packages without a valid PowerShell module manifest are rejected.
The caller supplies the private endpoint and credential independently to each command. PMU does not read an environment token, store credentials, or configure the repository.

maml:description.maml:para: Applies one live exact-version module update plan.

Revalidates and stages the exact package without importing it. Same-base replacement uses a verified backup, durable journal, exclusive OS handle lock, and best-effort rollback. Only provider-generated root PSGetModuleInfo.xml is excluded from SHA256 tree comparison. No module is hot reloaded. Interrupted operations require safe recovery and a fresh plan. The target is the compatible installed module bound by the plan, not necessarily the caller or a loaded module. No dependency on PMU is required.

An unmodified live `PSModuleUpdate.UpdatePlan` from this module instance. Pipeline binding is by value only; serialized and manufactured plans are rejected.

A schema-1 result reporting Outcome, ActiveVersion, InstalledVersion, TargetVersion, verification, dependency observations, recovery, and restart requirements independently. Outcomes are Installed, AlreadyInstalled, Cancelled, and WhatIf. Provider success alone never produces Installed.

maml:alert.maml:para:
Planning and WhatIf never perform recovery writes. After native approval, an exclusive OS handle lock covers revalidation, staging, backup, replacement, verification, rollback, and journal completion. Lock acquisition is bounded. The exact target and selected CurrentUser or AllUsers scope never change. AllUsers permission failures do not cause elevation or CurrentUser fallback. The exact registered source name, endpoint, API version, and trust state are revalidated before staging and again before installation. URI-selected plans do not re-resolve aliases if their bound registration disappears or changes. Production PMU never registers, repoints, or unregisters a repository.
Same-numeric-version prerelease progression uses exact Save-PSResource staging and internal Install-PSResource -Reinstall only for a validated collision. Backups are outside Modules. Journals use flushed temporary files and atomic file replacement; PMU does not claim atomic installation or guaranteed power-loss recovery. Interrupted state and journal paths are untrusted and validated before repair. Recovery that restores prior files requires a fresh plan. A complete target is recognized only after complete-tree verification.
TrustRepository is operation-scoped and never changes repository trust. AcceptLicense is independent of confirmation and trust. Missing or malformed provider license metadata conservatively requires explicit acceptance. Prerequisites are checked before quiet provider staging and installation, and checked again under the mutation lock. Direct credentials are never persisted or retained for later calls.
PMU does not import staged code or reload a consumer. RestartRequired includes replacement of loaded files even when version text is unchanged. When a newer target is installed while an older module remains loaded, restart is needed to use the target.
Stable error identifiers include PMU.InvalidPlan, PMU.PlanStale, PMU.RepositoryChanged, PMU.InstalledStateChanged, PMU.PermissionDenied, PMU.LockTimeout, PMU.VerificationFailed, PMU.RecoveryRequired, PMU.RecoveryFailed, and PMU.RollbackFailed. Preserve recovery evidence if repair cannot be verified. Recovery is impossible through this API when no matching module identity survives to satisfy Get-PSModuleUpdate's Module parameter.
Windows, Linux, PowerShell 7.4, real AllUsers writes, authenticated-feed installation, and later provider versions require separate qualification.

maml:introduction.maml:para: Revalidates read-only without locking, staging, installing, or repairing recovery state.
Requests native confirmation before applying the exact approved target and scope.
